1	#!/usr/bin/env bats
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# tests/unit/profile-floor.bats — cycle-129 sprint-256 Task 2.7 (AC-2.9; PRD
     4	# AC-9.2; SDD D-9.2, DEC-0166)
     5	#
     6	# No profile can reach the floor. The floor source is .claude/data/floor.yaml
     7	# (read here, never duplicated); its sha256 pin is READ from
     8	# tests/unit/guard-origins.bats (FLOOR_SHA256) so the two suites cannot
     9	# disagree. Under `lean` every floor surface reads byte-identically to
    10	# `standard`: the floor config keys (the two gate skills' flatline_protocol.*
    11	# config, destructive_command_guard.*, implement_gate.*, hounfour.locality),
    12	# verdict-derive.sh on fixture feedback files, the adversarial gate's
    13	# decision and environment, the deny-list file, the fence on the corpus and
    14	# the FR-1.2b / FR-SZ probes, and user-invoked-commands.txt.
    15	# =============================================================================
    16	
    17	bats_require_minimum_version 1.5.0
    18	
    19	setup() {
    20	    R="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/../.." && pwd)"
    21	    LIB="$R/.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh"
    22	    PROFILES="$R/.claude/data/profiles.yaml"
    23	    FLOOR="$R/.claude/data/floor.yaml"
    24	    T="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR"
    25	    # Two configs that differ ONLY in loa.profile: this repository's own config
    26	    # (which carries the floor keys it really uses) with the profile set.
    27	    for p in lean standard; do
    28	        cp "$R/.loa.config.yaml" "$T/$p.yaml"
    29	        yq -i ".loa.profile = \"$p\"" "$T/$p.yaml"
    30	    done
    31	    unset LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE LOA_PROFILES_FILE
    32	}
    33	
    34	# The floor key patterns, as the lib and the guard register read them.
    35	floor_keys() { yq -r '.floor_keys[]' "$FLOOR"; }
    36	
    37	@test "PF-1 floor.yaml matches the sha256 pin guard-origins.bats carries (one constant, two suites)" {
    38	    local pin actual
    39	    pin=$(sed -n 's/^FLOOR_SHA256="\([0-9a-f]\{64\}\)"$/\1/p' "$R/tests/unit/guard-origins.bats")
    40	    [ -n "$pin" ] || { echo "no FLOOR_SHA256 in guard-origins.bats"; return 1; }
    41	    actual=$(bash -c 'source "$1/.claude/scripts/compat-lib.sh"; sha256_portable "$2"' _ "$R" "$FLOOR" | cut -d' ' -f1)
    42	    [ "$actual" = "$pin" ] || { echo "floor.yaml sha256 $actual != pinned $pin"; return 1; }
    43	}
    44	
    45	@test "PF-2 no profiles.yaml key matches a floor key or is an ancestor of one" {
    46	    run python3 -I - "$PROFILES" "$FLOOR" <<'PY'
    47	import re, subprocess, sys, json
    48	def load(p):
    49	    return json.loads(subprocess.check_output(["yq", "-o=json", ".", p]))
    50	prof, floor = load(sys.argv[1]), load(sys.argv[2])
    51	keys = sorted({k for v in prof["profiles"].values() for k in v})
    52	assert len(keys) == 9, keys
    53	bad = []
    54	for k in keys:
    55	    for f in floor["floor_keys"]:
    56	        rx = "^" + ".+".join(re.escape(s) for s in f.split("*")) + "$"
    57	        if re.match(rx, k) or f.split("*")[0].startswith(k + "."):
    58	            bad.append((k, f))
    59	print("violations:", bad)
    60	sys.exit(1 if bad else 0)
    61	PY
    62	    echo "$output"
    63	    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    64	    # floor_keys_forbidden is not duplicated into profiles.yaml.
    65	    [ "$(yq -r 'has("floor_keys_forbidden")' "$PROFILES")" = "false" ]
    66	}
    67	
    68	@test "PF-3 under lean the resolved document names no floor key and every floor key reads as under standard" {
    69	    local p k
    70	    for p in lean standard; do
    71	        LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE="$T/$p.yaml" bash "$LIB" json > "$T/$p.json"
    72	        [ "$(jq -r '.profile' "$T/$p.json")" = "$p" ]
    73	    done
    74	    # Concrete floor keys: every leaf path of this config and the example that a
    75	    # floor pattern matches (flatline_protocol.*.companion_voice expands here).
    76	    yq -o=json '.' "$R/.loa.config.yaml" > "$T/cfg.json"
    77	    yq -o=json '.' "$R/.loa.config.yaml.example" > "$T/ex.json"
    78	    floor_keys > "$T/floor.txt"
    79	    python3 -I - "$T/cfg.json" "$T/ex.json" "$T/floor.txt" > "$T/concrete.txt" <<'PY'
    80	import json, re, sys
    81	pats = [l.strip() for l in open(sys.argv[3]) if l.strip()]
    82	rxs = ["^" + ".+".join(re.escape(s) for s in p.split("*")) + "$" for p in pats]
    83	out = set(p for p in pats if "*" not in p)
    84	def walk(x, path):
    85	    if isinstance(x, dict):
    86	        for k, v in x.items():
    87	            walk(v, path + [str(k)])
    88	    if path:
    89	        key = ".".join(path)
    90	        if any(re.match(r, key) for r in rxs):
    91	            out.add(key)
    92	for f in sys.argv[1:3]:
    93	    walk(json.load(open(f)), [])
    94	print("\n".join(sorted(k for k in out if re.fullmatch(r"[A-Za-z0-9_]+(\.[A-Za-z0-9_]+)*", k))))
    95	PY
    96	    grep -qx 'flatline_protocol.code_review.enabled' "$T/concrete.txt"
    97	    grep -qx 'flatline_protocol.security_audit.enabled' "$T/concrete.txt"
    98	    grep -q '^flatline_protocol\.[a-z_]*\.companion_voice$' "$T/concrete.txt"
    99	    while IFS= read -r k; do
   100	        [ "$(jq -r --arg k "$k" '.knobs | has($k)' "$T/lean.json")" = "false" ] || { echo "lean resolves floor key $k"; return 1; }
   101	        a=$(LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE="$T/lean.yaml" bash "$LIB" knob "$k" __unset__ 2>/dev/null)
   102	        b=$(LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE="$T/standard.yaml" bash "$LIB" knob "$k" __unset__ 2>/dev/null)
   103	        [ "$a" = "$b" ] || { echo "$k: lean=$a standard=$b"; return 1; }
   104	    done < "$T/concrete.txt"
   105	    # The two gate skills' whole flatline_protocol config is byte-identical.
   106	    for g in code_review security_audit; do
   107	        cmp <(yq -o=json ".flatline_protocol.$g" "$T/lean.yaml") <(yq -o=json ".flatline_protocol.$g" "$T/standard.yaml")
   108	    done
   109	}
   110	
   111	@test "PF-4 verdict-derive.sh output is byte-identical under lean and standard" {
   112	    local f p
   113	    printf 'All good\n\n## Observations\n\n- **LOW** `a.sh:1` — naming\n\n<!-- LOA-VERDICT {"gate":"review","verdict":"APPROVED","counts":{"critical":0,"high":0,"medium":0,"low":1},"sprint_id":"sprint-9","ts":"2026-10-14T00:00:00Z"} -->\n' > "$T/ok.md"
   114	    printf '## Changes Required\n\n- **HIGH** `a.sh:1` — unchecked input\n\nAll good\n\n<!-- LOA-VERDICT {"gate":"review","verdict":"APPROVED","counts":{"critical":0,"high":1,"medium":0,"low":0},"sprint_id":"sprint-9","ts":"2026-10-14T00:00:00Z"} -->\n' > "$T/bad.md"
   115	    for f in ok bad; do
   116	        for p in lean standard; do
   117	            rc=0
   118	            LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE="$T/$p.yaml" bash "$R/.claude/scripts/verdict-derive.sh" --file "$T/$f.md" --gate review --json \
   119	                > "$T/vd-$f-$p.out" 2>&1 || rc=$?
   120	            echo "$rc" >> "$T/vd-$f-$p.out"
   121	        done
   122	        cmp "$T/vd-$f-lean.out" "$T/vd-$f-standard.out"
   123	    done
   124	    # The fixtures exercise both outcomes, so identity is not vacuous.
   125	    ! cmp -s "$T/vd-ok-lean.out" "$T/vd-bad-lean.out"
   126	}
   127	
   128	@test "PF-5 the adversarial-review gate decides identically under lean and standard" {
   129	    local d="$T/grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-999" p rc
   130	    mkdir -p "$d"
   131	    for p in lean standard; do
   132	        yq -i '.flatline_protocol.code_review.enabled = true' "$T/$p.yaml"
   133	        rc=0
   134	        printf '{"tool_name":"Write","tool_input":{"file_path":"%s/COMPLETED"}}' "$d" \
   135	            | env -u LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_ENFORCE LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE="$T/$p.yaml" LOA_CONFIG_PATH_OVERRIDE="$T/$p.yaml" \
   136	              bash "$R/.claude/hooks/safety/adversarial-review-gate.sh" > "$T/gate-$p.out" 2>&1 || rc=$?
   137	        echo "$rc" >> "$T/gate-$p.out"
   138	    done
   139	    cmp "$T/gate-lean.out" "$T/gate-standard.out"
   140	    # No dissent envelope for an enabled gate: the gate refuses (exit 2) under both.
   141	    [ "$(tail -1 "$T/gate-lean.out")" = "2" ]
   142	    # The gate's environment knob is not a profile key and the gate never sources the lib.
   143	    ! grep -q 'profile-lib' "$R/.claude/hooks/safety/adversarial-review-gate.sh"
   144	    ! yq -r '.profiles[] | keys | .[]' "$PROFILES" | grep -qi 'adversarial'
   145	}
   146	
   147	@test "PF-6 the fence decides every corpus row and the FR-1.2b / FR-SZ probes identically under lean and standard" {
   148	    local p row cmd rc id
   149	    jq -r '.id' "$R/tests/fixtures/fence-corpus/corpus.jsonl" > /dev/null
   150	    # Floor probes (the corpus carries the floor rules named in floor.yaml floor_corpus when they exist).
   151	    printf '%s\n' \
   152	        '{"id":"FP-1","cmd":"git stash pop 2>/dev/null"}' \
   153	        '{"id":"FP-2","cmd":"git stash push -m x | tail -1"}' \
   154	        '{"id":"FP-3","cmd":"echo x > .claude/hooks/evil.sh"}' \
   155	        '{"id":"FP-4","cmd":"cp /tmp/a .claude/settings.json"}' \
   156	        '{"id":"FP-5","cmd":"sed -i s/a/b/ .claude/scripts/verdict-derive.sh"}' > "$T/probes.jsonl"
   157	    cat "$R/tests/fixtures/fence-corpus/corpus.jsonl" "$T/probes.jsonl" > "$T/all.jsonl"
   158	    for p in lean standard; do
   159	        mkdir -p "$T/root-$p/repo"
   160	        cp "$T/$p.yaml" "$T/root-$p/.loa.config.yaml"
   161	        : > "$T/fence-$p.txt"
   162	        while IFS= read -r row; do
   163	            [ -n "$row" ] || continue
   164	            id=$(jq -r '.id' <<<"$row"); cmd=$(jq -r '.cmd' <<<"$row")
   165	            rc=0
   166	            (cd "$T/root-$p/repo" && jq -cn --arg c "$cmd" '{tool_input: {command: $c}}' \
   167	                | env -u TMPDIR LOA_AUDIT_REPLAY=1 LOA_REPO_ROOT="$T/root-$p" LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE="$T/$p.yaml" \
   168	                  bash "$R/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1) || rc=$?
   169	            echo "$id $rc" >> "$T/fence-$p.txt"
   170	        done < "$T/all.jsonl"
   171	    done
   172	    cmp "$T/fence-lean.txt" "$T/fence-standard.txt"
   173	    for id in FP-1 FP-2 FP-3 FP-4 FP-5; do
   174	        grep -qx "$id 2" "$T/fence-lean.txt" || { echo "$id not blocked under lean: $(grep "^$id " "$T/fence-lean.txt")"; return 1; }
   175	    done
   176	    # Every floor_corpus row present in the corpus is in the compared set.
   177	    while IFS= read -r rule; do
   178	        jq -r --arg r "$rule" 'select(.rule == $r or (($r | endswith("*")) and (.rule | startswith($r | rtrimstr("*"))))) | .id' \
   179	            "$R/tests/fixtures/fence-corpus/corpus.jsonl" | while IFS= read -r id; do
   180	            grep -q "^$id " "$T/fence-lean.txt"
   181	        done
   182	    done < <(yq -r '.floor_corpus.rules[]' "$FLOOR")
   183	}
   184	
   185	@test "PF-7 the deny list, the System-Zone rules and user-invoked-commands.txt are untouched by resolving any profile" {

    22	  "simstim_constraints|.claude/skills/simstim-workflow/SKILL.md|skill-md-constraints.jq|[\"C-PHASE-002\",\"C-PHASE-003\",\"C-PHASE-004\",\"C-PHASE-007\",\"C-PHASE-008\",\"C-PROC-005\",\"C-PHASE-005\",\"C-PROC-002\",\"C-PROC-006\"] as \$o | [\$o[] as \$id | .constraints[] | select(.id == \$id)]"

    24	  "merge_constraints|.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md|claude-loa-md-table.jq|[.constraints[] | select(.layers[] | select(.section == \"merge_constraints\"))] | sort_by(.order)"

    39	# Utilities

    41

    44	pass() { echo "  PASS: $*"; }
    45	fail() { echo "  FAIL: $*"; ERRORS=$((ERRORS + 1)); }

    54	}

    59	
    60	check_registry_exists() {
    61	  log "Check 1: Registry exists and is valid JSON"
    62	
    63	  if [[ ! -f "$REGISTRY" ]]; then

    66	  fi

    71	  fi

    77	}

    81	# ============================================================================
    82	
    83	check_schema_compliance() {
    84	  log "Check 2: Schema compliance"
    85	
    86	  if [[ ! -f "$SCHEMA" ]]; then
    87	    fail "Schema not found: $SCHEMA"
    88	    return 1
    89	  fi

    94	      return 0
    95	    else
    96	      fail "Schema validation failed (ajv)"
    97	      return 1
    98	    fi
    99	  fi
   100	
   101	  # jq fallback: check required fields, ID patterns, enums
   102	  local errors=0
   103	
   104	  # Check top-level required fields
   105	  if ! jq -e '.version and .constraints' "$REGISTRY" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
   106	    fail "Missing required top-level fields (version, constraints)"
   107	    return 1
   108	  fi
   109	
   110	  # Check version pattern
   111	  local version
   112	  version=$(jq -r '.version' "$REGISTRY")
   113	  if ! [[ "$version" =~ ^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$ ]]; then
   114	    fail "Invalid version format: $version"
   115	    errors=$((errors + 1))
   116	  fi
   117	
   118	  # Check each constraint has required fields
   119	  local missing
   120	  missing=$(jq -r '
   121	    [.constraints[] | select(
   122	      (.id | not) or (.name | not) or (.category | not) or
   123	      (.rule_type | not) or (.text | not) or (.why | not) or
   124	      (.layers | not) or (.severity | not)
   125	    ) | .id // "UNKNOWN"] | join(", ")
   126	  ' "$REGISTRY")
   127	
   128	  if [[ -n "$missing" ]]; then
   129	    fail "Constraints missing required fields: $missing"
   130	    errors=$((errors + 1))
   131	  fi
   132	
   133	  # Check ID pattern

   405	  done
   406	}
   407

   409	  log "Checking for deprecated constraints"
   410	
   411	  local deprecated

   413	    [.constraints[] | select(.deprecated == true) |

   415	        active_layers: [.layers[] | select(.target != "error-code") | .target] | length }
   416	    ] | .[]

   418	  ' "$REGISTRY" 2>/dev/null)
   419	
   420	  if [[ -n "$deprecated" ]]; then
   421	    while IFS= read -r line; do
   422	      warn "Deprecated constraint with active layers: $line"
   423	    done <<< "$deprecated"
   424	  fi
   425	}
   426	
   427	# ============================================================================
   428	# Main
   429	# ============================================================================
   430	
   431	usage() {
   432	  cat <<'EOF'
   433	validate-constraints.sh — DRY Constraint Registry validator
   434	
   435	Usage: validate-constraints.sh [flags]
   436	
   437	Flags:
   438	  --verbose    Show detailed per-check output
   439	  --help       Show this help
   440	
   441	Exit codes:
   442	  0  All checks pass
   443	  1  One or more checks failed
   444	  2  Registry missing
   445	EOF
   446	}
   447	
   448	main() {
   449	  while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
   450	    case "$1" in
   451	      --verbose)  VERBOSE=true ;;
   452	      --help|-h)  usage; exit 0 ;;
   453	      *)          log "Unknown flag: $1"; exit 2 ;;
   454	    esac
   455	    shift
   456	  done
   457	
   458	  log "Validating constraint registry: $REGISTRY"
   459	  echo ""
   460	
   461	  # Check 1 is fatal — exit 2 if registry missing
   462	  if ! check_registry_exists; then
   463	    log "FATAL: Registry missing or invalid"
   464	    exit 2
   465	  fi
   466	
   467	  # Checks 2-8

   469	  check_unique_ids || true
   470	  check_error_code_refs || true
   471	  check_layer_coverage || true
   472	  check_target_files_exist || true
   473	  check_skill_names || true
   474	  check_section_freshness || true
   475	
   476	  echo ""
   477	
   478	  # Warning checks (non-fatal)
   479	  check_orphan_markers
   480	  check_deprecated_constraints
   481	
   482	  echo ""
   483	  log "Results: $ERRORS error(s), $WARNINGS warning(s)"
   484	
   485	  if [[ "$ERRORS" -gt 0 ]]; then
   486	    exit 1
   487	  fi
   488	  exit 0
   489	}
   490	
   491	main "$@"

# Review instructions

This workspace holds one pull request against the Loa framework repository, frozen for evaluation.

- `PR.md` — the PR title and description
- `head.diff` — the complete change (unified diff, base → head)
- `base/` — every touched file before the change
- `head/` — every touched file after the change

Review the change as the senior technical reviewer for this repository. There is no sprint plan, beads database, implementation report or `grimoires/loa/a2a/` directory here — the PR files above are the entire input; skip any pre-flight step that needs them and do not ask questions.

Write your review to `review.md` in this directory using the Write tool. Cite every finding as `head/<path>:<line>` with line numbers taken from the `head/` files. Follow your reviewer skill's output format and end the file with its machine-readable verdict trailer.

content.content:
# Audit instructions

This workspace holds one pull request against the Loa framework repository, frozen for evaluation.

- `PR.md` — the PR title and description
- `head.diff` — the complete change (unified diff, base → head)
- `base/` — every touched file before the change
- `head/` — every touched file after the change

Audit the change as the security auditor for this repository. There is no sprint plan, beads database, implementation report or `grimoires/loa/a2a/` directory here — the PR files above are the entire input; skip any pre-flight step that needs them and do not ask questions.

Write your audit to `audit.md` in this directory using the Write tool. Cite every finding as `head/<path>:<line>` with line numbers taken from the `head/` files. Follow your auditor skill's output format and end the file with its machine-readable verdict trailer.
# Review instructions

This workspace holds one pull request against the Loa framework repository, frozen for evaluation.

- `PR.md` — the PR title and description
- `head.diff` — the complete change (unified diff, base → head)
- `base/` — every touched file before the change

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# Lint Loa Structural Invariants
# =============================================================================
# Mechanically validates Loa's structural invariants. Run during /mount,
# /run preflight, /audit-sprint, or manually.
#
# Usage:
#   lint-invariants.sh              # Human-readable output
#   lint-invariants.sh --json       # Machine-readable JSON output
#   lint-invariants.sh --fix        # Auto-fix where possible
#
# Exit codes:
#   0 = all pass
#   1 = warnings only
#   2 = errors found
#
# Part of Loa Harness Engineering (cycle-011, issue #297)
# Source: OpenAI architectural invariants + custom linter pattern
# =============================================================================

set -euo pipefail

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Arguments
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
JSON_OUTPUT=false
AUTO_FIX=false
LINT_ROOT=""
HOOKS_WIRING_ONLY=false

while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case "$1" in
    --json) JSON_OUTPUT=true; shift ;;
    --fix) AUTO_FIX=true; shift ;;
    --root)
      # bug-1002: scan an alternate project root (tests use synthetic trees)
      [[ $# -ge 2 ]] || { echo "--root requires a value" >&2; exit 2; }
      LINT_ROOT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --hooks-wiring-only)
      # bug-1002: run only Invariant 7b (template<->live wiring parity)
      HOOKS_WIRING_ONLY=true; shift ;;
    -h|--help)
      echo "Usage: lint-invariants.sh [--json] [--fix] [--root DIR] [--hooks-wiring-only]"
      echo ""
      echo "  --json               Output results as JSON"
      echo "  --fix                Auto-fix where possible"
      echo "  --root DIR           Lint DIR instead of the current project"
      echo "  --hooks-wiring-only  Run only the hook wiring-parity invariant"
      exit 0
      ;;
    *) echo "Unknown option: $1" >&2; exit 1 ;;
  esac
done

if [[ -n "$LINT_ROOT" ]]; then
  # Audit iter (bug-1002): a full lint run EXECUTES scripts from the lint
  # target (Invariant 8 runs test-safety-hooks.sh) — running it against an
  # untrusted checkout would execute attacker-controlled code. --root is
  # only safe for the read-only wiring check.
  # the re-stamp signal too.
  if head -1 "$file" | grep -q 'PLACEHOLDER'; then
    report "WARN" "claude-md" "CLAUDE.loa.md header carries a PLACEHOLDER residue — re-stamp via .claude/scripts/marker-utils.sh update-hash"
  fi
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Invariant 3: constraints.json is valid JSON
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
check_constraints() {
  local file=".claude/data/constraints.json"

  if [[ ! -f "$file" ]]; then
    report "WARN" "constraints" "constraints.json not found at $file"
    return
  fi

  if jq empty "$file" 2>/dev/null; then
    report "PASS" "constraints" "constraints.json is valid JSON"
  else
    report "ERROR" "constraints" "constraints.json is invalid JSON"
    if [[ "$AUTO_FIX" == "true" ]]; then
      echo "  Cannot auto-fix invalid JSON — manual repair needed"
    fi
  fi
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Invariant 4: Constraint-generated blocks exist in CLAUDE.loa.md
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
check_constraint_blocks() {
  local file=".claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"

  if [[ ! -f "$file" ]]; then
    report "ERROR" "constraint-blocks" "CLAUDE.loa.md not found"
    return
  fi

  local block_count
  block_count=$(grep -c '@constraint-generated: start' "$file" 2>/dev/null || true)
  [[ -z "$block_count" ]] && block_count=0

  if [[ "$block_count" -ge 3 ]]; then
    report "PASS" "constraint-blocks" "$block_count constraint-generated blocks found"
  elif [[ "$block_count" -gt 0 ]]; then
    report "WARN" "constraint-blocks" "Only $block_count constraint-generated blocks (expected 3+)"
  else
    report "ERROR" "constraint-blocks" "No constraint-generated blocks found"
  fi

  # Check start/end pairs match
  local start_count end_count
  start_count=$(grep -c '@constraint-generated: start' "$file" 2>/dev/null || true)
  end_count=$(grep -c '@constraint-generated: end' "$file" 2>/dev/null || true)
  [[ -z "$start_count" ]] && start_count=0
  [[ -z "$end_count" ]] && end_count=0

  if [[ "$start_count" -ne "$end_count" ]]; then
    report "ERROR" "constraint-blocks" "Mismatched start/end pairs: $start_count starts, $end_count ends"
  fi
}

compute_section_hash() {
  # SHA-256, first 16 chars, LF-normalized, trailing whitespace trimmed
  printf '%s' "$1" \
    | tr -d '\r' \
    | sed 's/[[:space:]]*$//' \
    | sha256_portable \
    | cut -c1-16
}

# ============================================================================
# Registry validation
# ============================================================================

validate_registry() {
  if [[ ! -f "$REGISTRY" ]]; then
    die "Registry not found: $REGISTRY"
  fi

  if ! jq empty "$REGISTRY" 2>/dev/null; then
    die "Registry is not valid JSON: $REGISTRY"
  fi

  # Check for duplicate IDs
  local dupes
  dupes=$(jq -r '[.constraints[].id] | sort | group_by(.) | map(select(length > 1)) | length' "$REGISTRY")
  if [[ "$dupes" -gt 0 ]]; then
    die "Registry has duplicate constraint IDs"
  fi

  verbose "Registry validated: $(jq '.constraints | length' "$REGISTRY") constraints"
}

# ============================================================================
# Rendering
# ============================================================================

render_section() {
  local section_name="$1"
  local template="$2"
  local filter_jq="$3"

  local template_file="${TEMPLATE_DIR}/${template}"
  if [[ ! -f "$template_file" ]]; then
    die "Template not found: $template_file"
  fi

  jq -r "$filter_jq" "$REGISTRY" | jq -r -f "$template_file"
}

# ============================================================================
# Section insertion
# ============================================================================

insert_generated_section() {
  local file="$1"
  local section="$2"
  local content="$3"

  local hash
  hash=$(compute_section_hash "$content")

  local start_marker="<!-- @constraint-generated: start ${section} | hash:${hash} -->"
  local end_marker="<!-- @constraint-generated: end ${section} -->"
  local warning="<!-- DO NOT EDIT — generated from .claude/data/constraints.json -->"

  if grep -q "@constraint-generated: start ${section}" "$file"; then
    # Replace content between existing markers
    local tmp="${file}.gen-tmp"
    awk -v start="@constraint-generated: start ${section}" \
        -v end="@constraint-generated: end ${section}" \
        -v new_start="$start_marker" \
        -v new_warning="$warning" \
        -v new_content="$content" \
        -v new_end="$end_marker" \
        '
        $0 ~ start { print new_start; print new_warning; printf "%s\n", new_content; skip=1; next }
        $0 ~ end   { print new_end; skip=0; next }
        !skip       { print }
        ' "$file" > "$tmp"
    mv "$tmp" "$file"
  else
    log "ERROR: Missing markers in ${file} for section '${section}'. Run with --bootstrap --confirm to insert."
    return 1
  fi
}

# ============================================================================
# Bootstrap: insert markers into target files
# ============================================================================

# Anchor patterns: section_name|start_regex|end_regex
readonly -a ANCHORS=(
  "process_compliance_never|^### NEVER Rules$|^### |^---$"
  "process_compliance_always|^### ALWAYS Rules$|^### |^---$"
  "task_tracking_hierarchy|^### Task Tracking Hierarchy$|^$|^---$"
  "pre_implementation_checklist|^## Pre-Implementation Checklist$|^## |^---$"
  "autonomous_agent_constraints|AUTONOMOUS_SKILL_ANCHOR|AUTONOMOUS_SKILL_END"
  "simstim_constraints|SIMSTIM_SKILL_ANCHOR|SIMSTIM_SKILL_END"
  "implementing_tasks_constraints|IMPLEMENTING_SKILL_ANCHOR|IMPLEMENTING_SKILL_END"
)

bootstrap_section() {
  local file="$1"
  local section="$2"
  local content="$3"

  local hash
  hash=$(compute_section_hash "$content")

  local start_marker="<!-- @constraint-generated: start ${section} | hash:${hash} -->"
  local end_marker="<!-- @constraint-generated: end ${section} -->"
  local warning="<!-- DO NOT EDIT — generated from .claude/data/constraints.json -->"

  if grep -q "@constraint-generated: start ${section}" "$file"; then
    verbose "Section ${section} already has markers in ${file}, skipping bootstrap"
    return 0
  fi

  # Find anchor for this section
  local anchor_start="" anchor_end=""
  for anchor in "${ANCHORS[@]}"; do
    local a_section a_start a_end
    IFS='|' read -r a_section a_start a_end <<< "$anchor"
    if [[ "$a_section" == "$section" ]]; then
      anchor_start="$a_start"
      anchor_end="$a_end"
      break
    fi
  done

  if [[ -z "$anchor_start" ]]; then
    log "WARNING: No anchor defined for section ${section}, skipping"
    return 0
  fi

  # For skill-md sections, use <constraints> tags
  if [[ "$anchor_start" == *"SKILL_ANCHOR"* ]]; then
    verbose "Skill section ${section}: markers will be inserted inside <constraints> block during generation"
    return 0
  fi

  # Find the anchor line and insert markers after the table header
  local matches
  matches=$(grep -c "$anchor_start" "$file" 2>/dev/null || echo "0")
  if [[ "$matches" -ne 1 ]]; then
    log "ERROR: Anchor '${anchor_start}' matches ${matches} times in ${file} (expected 1)"
    return 1
  fi

  # Find the section: locate header, keep table header+separator, wrap data rows with markers
  local tmp="${file}.bootstrap-tmp"
  local end_pat1="${anchor_end%%|*}"
  local end_pat2="${anchor_end#*|}"
  awk -v anchor="$anchor_start" \
      -v end_pat1="$end_pat1" \
      -v end_pat2="$end_pat2" \
      -v start_m="$start_marker" \
      -v warning_m="$warning" \
      -v end_m="$end_marker" \
      -v content_m="$content" \
      '
      BEGIN { state="looking"; sep_seen=0 }
      state == "looking" && $0 ~ anchor {
        print; state="in_header"; next
      }
      state == "in_header" {
        # Print everything until we see the separator row (|---|)
        print
        if ($0 ~ /^\|[-|: ]+\|$/) {
          sep_seen=1
          print start_m
          print warning_m
          printf "%s\n", content_m
          state="skipping"
        }
        next
      }
      state == "skipping" {
        if ($0 ~ end_pat1 || $0 ~ end_pat2) {
          print end_m
          if ($0 !~ /^$/) print
          state="done"
          next
        }
        # Skip original data rows (replaced by generated content)
        next
      }
      state != "skipping" { print }
      END {
        if (state == "skipping") print end_m
      }
      ' "$file" > "$tmp"

  if [[ "$DRY_RUN" == "true" ]] && [[ "$BOOTSTRAP_CONFIRM" != "true" ]]; then
    diff -u "$file" "$tmp" || true
    rm -f "$tmp"
  else
    mv "$tmp" "$file"
    log "Bootstrapped markers for section '${section}' in ${file}"
  fi
}

# ============================================================================
# Main generation pipeline
# ============================================================================

generate_all_sections() {
  # Phase 0: Build target -> sections map
  declare -A target_sections
  declare -A section_data  # section -> "target|template|filter"

  for entry in "${SECTIONS[@]}"; do
    local s_name s_target s_template s_filter
    IFS='|' read -r s_name s_target s_template s_filter <<< "$entry"

    if [[ -n "$SECTION_FILTER" ]] && [[ "$s_name" != "$SECTION_FILTER" ]]; then
      continue
    fi

    if [[ ! -f "$s_target" ]]; then
      log "WARNING: Target file not found: $s_target, skipping"
      continue
    fi

    target_sections["$s_target"]+="${s_name} "
    section_data["$s_name"]="${s_target}|${s_template}|${s_filter}"
  done

  if [[ ${#target_sections[@]} -eq 0 ]]; then
    log "No sections to generate"
    return 0
  fi

  # Phase 1: Create staged copies
  declare -A staged_files
  trap 'for tmp in "${staged_files[@]}"; do rm -f "$tmp"; done' EXIT

  for target in "${!target_sections[@]}"; do
    local tmp
    tmp=$(mktemp "${target}.constraint-XXXXXX")
    cp "$target" "$tmp"
    staged_files["$target"]="$tmp"
  done

  # Phase 2: Render and apply all sections to staged copies
  for target in "${!target_sections[@]}"; do
    local tmp="${staged_files[$target]}"
    for section in ${target_sections[$target]}; do
      local s_data="${section_data[$section]}"
      local s_target s_template s_filter
      IFS='|' read -r s_target s_template s_filter <<< "$s_data"

      local o_heading
      if o_heading=$(optional_table_heading "$section"); then
        local o_rows
        o_rows=$(jq -r "$s_filter | length" "$REGISTRY")
        if [[ "$o_rows" == "0" ]]; then
          if [[ "$BOOTSTRAP" != "true" ]] && ! prune_optional_table "$tmp" "$section" "$o_heading"; then
            log "ERROR: Generation failed for section '${section}' — no files modified"
            return 1
          fi
          continue
        fi
      fi

      verbose "Rendering section: $section"
      local content
      content=$(render_section "$section" "$s_template" "$s_filter")

      if [[ "$BOOTSTRAP" == "true" ]]; then
        bootstrap_section "$tmp" "$section" "$content"
      else
        if ! insert_generated_section "$tmp" "$section" "$content"; then
          log "ERROR: Generation failed for section '${section}' — no files modified"
          return 1
        fi
      fi

    done

    trap - EXIT

    backup_files["$target"]="$bak"

    else

      break
    fi

    local rollback_ok=true
    for t in "${committed[@]}"; do
      if ! cp -f "${backup_files[$t]}" "$t"; then

      fi

    fi

    return 1
  fi

    fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# Invariant Linter Self-Test — "Who Tests the Testers?"
# =============================================================================
# Test harness for lint-invariants.sh itself. Creates temp fixtures with
# known-good and known-bad states, runs the linter, validates output.
#
# Follows the LLVM principle: test the test infrastructure.
#
# Usage:
#   bash .claude/scripts/test-lint-invariants.sh
#   bash .claude/scripts/test-lint-invariants.sh --verbose
#
# Exit codes:
#   0 = all tests pass
#   1 = one or more tests failed
#
# Source: Bridgebuilder Deep Review Critical 3
# Part of Loa Harness Engineering (cycle-011, issue #297)
# =============================================================================

set -uo pipefail

# Resolve absolute path to linter before any cd operations
LINTER_ABS="$(cd "$(dirname ".claude/scripts/lint-invariants.sh")" && pwd)/$(basename ".claude/scripts/lint-invariants.sh")"
PASS=0
FAIL=0
TOTAL=0
VERBOSE=false
TMPDIR_BASE=""

[[ "${1:-}" == "--verbose" ]] && VERBOSE=true

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Setup / Teardown
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
setup_tmpdir() {
  TMPDIR_BASE=$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/lint-invariant-test.XXXXXX")
}

teardown_tmpdir() {
  if [[ -n "$TMPDIR_BASE" && -d "$TMPDIR_BASE" ]]; then
    rm -rf "$TMPDIR_BASE"
  fi
}

trap teardown_tmpdir EXIT

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Test helpers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
assert_exit_code() {
  local actual="$1"
  local expected="$2"
  local desc="$3"

  TOTAL=$((TOTAL + 1))
  if [[ "$actual" -eq "$expected" ]]; then
    PASS=$((PASS + 1))
    [[ "$VERBOSE" == "true" ]] && printf "  [PASS] %s\n" "$desc"
  local output="$1"
  local desc="$2"

  TOTAL=$((TOTAL + 1))
  if echo "$output" | jq empty 2>/dev/null; then
    PASS=$((PASS + 1))
    [[ "$VERBOSE" == "true" ]] && printf "  [PASS] %s\n" "$desc"
  else
    FAIL=$((FAIL + 1))
    printf "  [FAIL] %s (invalid JSON)\n" "$desc"
  fi
}

# Run linter in a directory, capturing output and exit code separately
run_linter_in() {
  local dir="$1"
  shift
  # Run in subshell, capture output. Use explicit exit code capture.
  local output exit_code
  output=$(cd "$dir" && bash "$LINTER_ABS" "$@" 2>&1) && exit_code=0 || exit_code=$?
  echo "$exit_code"
  echo "---OUTPUT---"
  echo "$output"
}

parse_result() {
  local result="$1"
  RESULT_EXIT=$(echo "$result" | head -1)
  RESULT_OUTPUT=$(echo "$result" | sed '1d;/^---OUTPUT---$/d')
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Create a minimal known-good project fixture
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
create_good_fixture() {
  local dir="$1"
  mkdir -p "$dir/.claude/loa" "$dir/.claude/data" "$dir/.claude/hooks/safety" "$dir/.claude/hooks/audit" "$dir/.claude/hooks" "$dir/.claude/scripts"

  # CLAUDE.loa.md with managed header and constraint blocks
  cat > "$dir/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md" << 'MDEOF'
<!-- @loa-managed: true | version: 1.34.0 | hash: testfixture -->

# Loa Framework Instructions

## Process Compliance

### NEVER Rules
<!-- @constraint-generated: start process_compliance_never | hash:test -->
| Rule |
<!-- @constraint-generated: end process_compliance_never -->

### ALWAYS Rules
<!-- @constraint-generated: start process_compliance_always | hash:test -->
| Rule |
<!-- @constraint-generated: end process_compliance_always -->

### Task Tracking
<!-- @constraint-generated: start task_tracking_hierarchy | hash:test -->
| Tool |
<!-- @constraint-generated: end task_tracking_hierarchy -->
MDEOF

  # Version file
  echo '{"version": "1.34.0"}' > "$dir/.loa-version.json"

  # Config file
  echo "run_mode:" > "$dir/.loa.config.yaml"
  echo "  enabled: true" >> "$dir/.loa.config.yaml"

  # Constraints JSON
  echo '{"constraints": []}' > "$dir/.claude/data/constraints.json"

  # settings.hooks.json
  cat > "$dir/.claude/hooks/settings.hooks.json" << 'HOOKEOF'
{"hooks":{"PreToolUse":[{"matcher":"Bash","hooks":[{"type":"command","command":"test"}]}],"PostToolUse":[{"matcher":"Bash","hooks":[{"type":"command","command":"test"}]}],"Stop":[{"matcher":"","hooks":[{"type":"command","command":"test"}]}]}}
HOOKEOF

  # Hook scripts (executable)
  for f in pre-compact-marker.sh post-compact-reminder.sh; do
    echo '#!/usr/bin/env bash' > "$dir/.claude/hooks/$f"
    chmod +x "$dir/.claude/hooks/$f"
  done
  echo '#!/usr/bin/env bash' > "$dir/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh"
  chmod +x "$dir/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh"
  echo '#!/usr/bin/env bash' > "$dir/.claude/hooks/safety/run-mode-stop-guard.sh"
  chmod +x "$dir/.claude/hooks/safety/run-mode-stop-guard.sh"
  echo '#!/usr/bin/env bash' > "$dir/.claude/hooks/audit/mutation-logger.sh"
  chmod +x "$dir/.claude/hooks/audit/mutation-logger.sh"

  # Stub test scripts so invariants 8/9 find them
  # Safety hook test: always pass (stub)
  cat > "$dir/.claude/scripts/test-safety-hooks.sh" << 'STUBEOF'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
exit 0
STUBEOF
  chmod +x "$dir/.claude/scripts/test-safety-hooks.sh"

  # Deny rule verify: always pass (stub)
  cat > "$dir/.claude/scripts/verify-deny-rules.sh" << 'STUBEOF'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
exit 0
STUBEOF
  chmod +x "$dir/.claude/scripts/verify-deny-rules.sh"

  # Initialize git repo so system-zone check works
  (cd "$dir" && git init -q && git add -A && git commit -q -m "init" 2>/dev/null) || true
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Create a known-bad fixture (missing files, invalid JSON)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
create_bad_fixture() {
  local dir="$1"
  mkdir -p "$dir/.claude/loa" "$dir/.claude/data" "$dir/.claude/hooks"

  # CLAUDE.loa.md without managed header, no constraint blocks
  echo "# Bad CLAUDE.loa.md" > "$dir/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"

  # Missing .loa-version.json (intentionally)

  # Config file
  echo "run_mode:" > "$dir/.loa.config.yaml"

  # Invalid JSON for constraints
  echo "not valid json" > "$dir/.claude/data/constraints.json"

  # settings.hooks.json (valid but minimal)
  echo '{"hooks":{}}' > "$dir/.claude/hooks/settings.hooks.json"

  # Initialize git
  (cd "$dir" && git init -q && git add -A && git commit -q -m "init" 2>/dev/null) || true
}

echo "Invariant Linter Self-Test"
echo "=========================="
echo "Linter: $LINTER_ABS"
echo ""

if [[ ! -f "$LINTER_ABS" ]]; then
  echo "ERROR: Linter not found at $LINTER_ABS"
  exit 1
fi

setup_tmpdir

# =========================================================================
# Test 1: Good fixture — all pass (exit 0 or 1 with WARNs)
# =========================================================================
echo "--- Test: Known-good fixture ---"
good_dir="$TMPDIR_BASE/good"
create_good_fixture "$good_dir"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# generate-constraints.sh — DRY Constraint Registry generator
# Reads constraints.json, renders via jq templates, updates target files
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
# shellcheck source=bash-version-guard.sh
source "$SCRIPT_DIR/bash-version-guard.sh"
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/compat-lib.sh"

# Constants
readonly REGISTRY=".claude/data/constraints.json"
readonly SCHEMA=".claude/schemas/constraints.schema.json"
readonly TEMPLATE_DIR=".claude/templates/constraints"
readonly MARKER_UTILS="${SCRIPT_DIR}/marker-utils.sh"

# Section definitions: section_name|target_file|template|filter_jq
readonly -a SECTIONS=(
  "process_compliance_never|.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md|claude-loa-md-table.jq|[.constraints[] | select(.layers[] | select(.section == \"process_compliance_never\"))] | sort_by(.order)"
  "process_compliance_always|.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md|claude-loa-md-table.jq|[.constraints[] | select(.layers[] | select(.section == \"process_compliance_always\"))] | sort_by(.order)"
  "task_tracking_hierarchy|.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md|task-tracking.jq|[.constraints[] | select(.layers[] | select(.section == \"task_tracking_hierarchy\"))] | sort_by(.order)"
  "pre_implementation_checklist|.claude/protocols/implementation-compliance.md|protocol-checklist.jq|[\"C-PROC-008\",\"C-PROC-006\",\"C-PROC-009\",\"C-PROC-010\",\"C-GIT-001\",\"C-PROC-005\"] as \$o | [\$o[] as \$id | .constraints[] | select(.id == \$id)]"
# no rows, the whole block (the heading, the table header, the marker block and
# one trailing blank line) is removed from the target instead of rendering an
# empty table (cycle-129 D-4.5). Restoring rows later needs the heading block
# back first (`--bootstrap` cannot re-create a heading): insert_generated_section
# then fails with "Missing markers", naming the section.
readonly -a OPTIONAL_TABLES=(
  "agent_teams_constraints|## Agent Teams"
)

# Flags
DRY_RUN=false
VERBOSE=false
VALIDATE_ONLY=false
BOOTSTRAP=false
BOOTSTRAP_CONFIRM=false
SECTION_FILTER=""

# ============================================================================
# Utilities
# ============================================================================

log() { echo "[generate-constraints] $*" >&2; }
verbose() { [[ "$VERBOSE" == "true" ]] && log "$@" || true; }
  log "Generation complete: ${#target_sections[@]} target(s) updated"
}

# ============================================================================
# Argument parsing
# ============================================================================

parse_args() {
  while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    case "$1" in
      --dry-run)     DRY_RUN=true ;;
      --verbose)     VERBOSE=true ;;
      --validate-only) VALIDATE_ONLY=true ;;
      --section)     shift; SECTION_FILTER="${1:-}"; [[ -z "$SECTION_FILTER" ]] && die "--section requires a name" ;;
      --bootstrap)   BOOTSTRAP=true; DRY_RUN=true ;;
      --confirm)     BOOTSTRAP_CONFIRM=true; DRY_RUN=false ;;
      --help|-h)     usage; exit 0 ;;
      *)             die "Unknown flag: $1" ;;
    esac
    shift
  done

  # --bootstrap --confirm: bootstrap with actual writes
  if [[ "$BOOTSTRAP" == "true" ]] && [[ "$BOOTSTRAP_CONFIRM" == "true" ]]; then
    DRY_RUN=false
  fi
}

usage() {
  cat <<'EOF'
generate-constraints.sh — DRY Constraint Registry generator

Usage: generate-constraints.sh [flags]

Flags:
  --dry-run          Print diff to stdout, don't write files
  --verbose          Print per-section rendering details
  --validate-only    Check staleness without writing
  --section NAME     Regenerate only the named section
  --bootstrap        Show where markers would be inserted (implies --dry-run)
  --confirm          Used with --bootstrap to actually write markers
  --help             Show this help

Exit codes:
  0  Success
  1  Validation error
  2  Registry error
EOF
}

# ============================================================================
# Main
# ============================================================================

main() {
  parse_args "$@"

  if [[ "$VALIDATE_ONLY" == "true" ]]; then
    exec bash "${SCRIPT_DIR}/validate-constraints.sh"
  fi

  validate_registry
  generate_all_sections
}

main "$@"

    fi

    # --- Cost-profile correlation check (SDD §3.4) ---
    if [[ "$cp" == "lightweight" && "$caps" != "null" && "$caps" != "all" ]]; then
        local wf
        wf=$(echo "$frontmatter" | yq eval '.capabilities.write_files' - 2>/dev/null) || wf="null"
        if [[ "$wf" == "true" ]]; then
            log_warning "$skill_name" "cost-profile: lightweight but capabilities.write_files: true (correlation mismatch)" || has_error=true
        fi
    fi

    # --- cycle-114 FR-3: optional `effort:` validation ---
    # effort is optional. When present it must be a valid level. A
    # deep-reasoning (xhigh/max) effort paired with a lightweight cost-profile
    # is a suspicious combination (cheap-tier skill asking for the deepest
    # reasoning) → WARN, not ERROR.
    local effort
    effort=$(echo "$frontmatter" | yq eval '.effort // ""' - 2>/dev/null) || effort=""
    if [[ -n "$effort" ]]; then
        local effort_valid=false
        local e
        for e in "${VALID_EFFORTS[@]}"; do
            [[ "$effort" == "$e" ]] && effort_valid=true && break
        done
        if [[ "$effort_valid" == "false" ]]; then
            log_error "$skill_name" "Invalid effort '$effort' (must be one of: ${VALID_EFFORTS[*]}) — cycle-114 FR-3"
            has_error=true
        elif [[ "$cp" == "lightweight" && ( "$effort" == "xhigh" || "$effort" == "max" ) ]]; then
            log_warning "$skill_name" "cost-profile: lightweight but effort: $effort (deep reasoning on a cheap-tier skill — correlation mismatch)" || has_error=true

    # A role:review skill that can write_files but neither disallows Write nor
    # is a documented write-exception leaves C-PROC-001 ("no application code
    # outside /implement") enforced only by prose. Surface that gap as a WARN.
    local fr4_role

        if [[ "$fr4_wf" == "true" ]]; then
            local disallowed
            disallowed=$(echo "$frontmatter" | yq eval '(.disallowed-tools // []) | join(",")' - 2>/dev/null) || disallowed=""
            local is_exception=false
            local x
            for x in "${REVIEW_WRITE_EXCEPTIONS[@]}"; do

            if [[ "$is_exception" == "false" ]] && ! has_tool "$disallowed" "Write"; then

        # Read without `//` (yq's alternative operator treats an explicit
        # false as absent); accept the list or the comma-string form.
        local pr_wf pr_dis pr_missing="" pr_t
        pr_wf=$(echo "$frontmatter" | yq eval '.capabilities.write_files' - 2>/dev/null) || pr_wf="null"
        if [[ "$pr_wf" == "false" ]]; then
            pr_dis=$(echo "$frontmatter" | yq eval '.disallowed-tools | ((select(tag == "!!seq") | join(",")) // .)' - 2>/dev/null) || pr_dis=""

                has_tool "$pr_dis" "$pr_t" || pr_missing+="${pr_missing:+, }$pr_t"

log_pass() {
    local skill="$1"
    passed=$((passed + 1))
    if [[ "$JSON_OUTPUT" == "false" ]]; then
        echo -e "  ${GREEN}PASS${NC}"
    fi
}

# --- Capability-to-tool mapping (SDD §3.3) ---
# Returns 0 if tool is in allowed-tools
has_tool() {
    local allowed="$1" tool="$2"
    # Use word-boundary matching to prevent substring false positives
    # (e.g., "WriteConfig" should not match "Write")
    echo "$allowed" | grep -qiwF "$tool"
}

# # ICM-L2-INPUTS-LINT: ICM Layer-2 advisory inputs manifest rot-lint.
# Reads the optional top-level `inputs:` frontmatter list (each entry: path[, why]).
# For each DECLARED path, WARNs (advisory only) if it is absent on disk — a drift
# signal that the skill's known-failures-first / context inputs have moved. It NEVER
# flags an undeclared read and NEVER fails the build. Absence of a manifest is fine.
validate_skill_inputs() {
    local skill_name="$1" frontmatter="$2"
    local inputs_raw n i p
    inputs_raw=$(echo "$frontmatter" | yq eval '.inputs' - 2>/dev/null) || inputs_raw="null"
    [[ "$inputs_raw" == "null" || -z "$inputs_raw" ]] && return 0
    local itype; itype=$(echo "$frontmatter" | yq eval '.inputs | type' - 2>/dev/null) || itype=""
    [[ "$itype" == "!!seq" ]] || { log_advisory "$skill_name" "inputs: is not a list (manifest ignored)"; return 0; }
    n=$(echo "$frontmatter" | yq eval '.inputs | length' - 2>/dev/null) || n=0
    [[ "$n" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || return 0
    for ((i=0; i<n; i++)); do
        p=$(echo "$frontmatter" | yq eval ".inputs[$i].path // \"\"" - 2>/dev/null) || p=""
        if [[ -z "$p" ]]; then
            log_advisory "$skill_name" "inputs[$i] declares no 'path' (advisory manifest entry ignored)"

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# tools/check-knob-readers.sh — no direct read of a profile key outside
     4	# profile-lib.sh (cycle-129 SDD D-9.1, sprint-256 Task 2.7).
     5	#
     6	# Every key under any profile in .claude/data/profiles.yaml must be read
     7	# through `loa_knob` (.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh), never by a reader's
     8	# own `yq '.<key> // <default>'`: a direct read skips the profile, and yq's
     9	# `//` reads an explicit `false` as absent. The check flags a line that names a
    10	# profile key in yq-path form (a leading dot: `.guardrails.input.enabled`)
    11	# under .claude/ (scripts, hooks, skills, data) and tools/, except
    12	# profile-lib.sh itself. Prose that names a key without the dot
    13	# (`guardrails.input.enabled: false`) is not a read and is not flagged.
    14	#
    15	# Misses: a key assembled at runtime (".guardrails.input.${x}.enabled") and a
    16	# reader in a language that indexes the config as nested keys.
    17	#
    18	# Usage: tools/check-knob-readers.sh [--root DIR]
    19	# Exit:  0 clean · 1 direct read found (each printed as path:line) · 2 usage
    20	# =============================================================================
    21	set -euo pipefail
    22	export LC_ALL=C
    23	
    24	ROOT="."
    25	while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    26	  case "$1" in
    27	    --root) [[ $# -ge 2 ]] || { echo "check-knob-readers.sh: --root needs a directory" >&2; exit 2; }; ROOT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    28	    -h|--help) sed -n '/^# Usage:/,/^# Exit:/p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; exit 0 ;;
    29	    *) echo "check-knob-readers.sh: unknown arg $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
    30	  esac
    31	done
    32	PROFILES="$ROOT/.claude/data/profiles.yaml"
    33	[[ -f "$PROFILES" ]] || { echo "check-knob-readers.sh: $PROFILES not found" >&2; exit 2; }
    34	command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "check-knob-readers.sh: yq v4 required" >&2; exit 2; }
    35	
    36	keys=$(yq -r '.profiles[] | keys | .[]' "$PROFILES" | sort -u)
    37	[[ -n "$keys" ]] || { echo "check-knob-readers.sh: no profile keys in $PROFILES" >&2; exit 2; }
    38	# Alternation of the dot-escaped keys; each must be preceded by a dot that is
    39	# not itself part of an identifier (start of line, quote, space, paren, ...).
    40	alt=$(printf '%s\n' "$keys" | sed 's/\./\\./g' | paste -sd'|' -)
    41	pattern="(^|[^A-Za-z0-9_])\\.(${alt})([^A-Za-z0-9_]|$)"
    42	
    43	hits=$(cd "$ROOT" && grep -rnE "$pattern" .claude tools 2>/dev/null \
    44	  | grep -v -E '^(\./)?\.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib\.sh:' \
    45	  | grep -v -E '^(\./)?tools/check-knob-readers\.sh:' || true)
    46	if [[ -n "$hits" ]]; then
    47	  echo "check-knob-readers.sh: direct read(s) of a profile key; use loa_knob from .claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh:" >&2
    48	  printf '%s\n' "$hits" | cut -c1-240 >&2
    49	  exit 1
    50	fi
    51	echo "check-knob-readers.sh: no direct profile-key reads ($(printf '%s\n' "$keys" | wc -l | tr -d ' ') keys checked)"

# run-mode state-file schemas (cycle-121 split from SKILL.md)

Exact JSON shapes for .run/ state files. SKILL.md's procedures reference these by section name; write files with these exact keys.

## run-state-schema

```json
{
  "run_id": "run-20260119-abc123",
  "target": "sprint-1",
  "branch": "feature/sprint-1",
  "state": "JACK_IN",
  "phase": "INIT",
  "timestamps": {
    "started": "2026-01-19T10:00:00Z",
    "last_activity": "2026-01-19T11:30:00Z"
  },
  "cycles": {
    "current": 0,
    "limit": 20,
    "history": []
  },
  "metrics": {
    "files_changed": 0,
    "files_deleted": 0,
    "commits": 0,
    "findings_fixed": 0
  },
  "options": {
    "max_cycles": 20,
    "timeout_hours": 8,
    "dry_run": false,
    "local_mode": false,
    "confirm_push": false,
    "push_mode": "AUTO"
  },
  "completion": {
    "pushed": false,
    "pr_created": false,
    "pr_url": null,
    "skipped_reason": null
  }
}
```

## circuit-breaker-schema

```json
{
  "state": "CLOSED",
  "triggers": {
    "same_issue": {"count": 0, "threshold": 3, "last_hash": null},
    "no_progress": {"count": 0, "threshold": 5},
    "cycle_count": {"current": 0, "limit": 20},
    "timeout": {"started": "2026-01-19T10:00:00Z", "limit_hours": 8}
  },
  "history": []
}
```

Written by `run-checkpoint.sh record-round` (one call per review/audit verdict) and recomputed by
`run-checkpoint.sh derive` (counters raised from the feedback history, never lowered). They add
`triggers.no_progress.last_counts` (the previous round's counts), `last_round`, `last_trip` and,
after `/run-resume --reset-ice`, `reset_at` (rounds before it no longer count).

## red-team-code-state

```json
{

`schema_version` 2 (cycle-125 FR-3) adds `checkpoint` — written only by
`.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh write` (atomic, locked); `task` is the last CLOSED bead
(`null` for a phase-only checkpoint). Readers accept 1 and 2; a missing or discarded checkpoint
means sprint granularity (resume at the first open bead of `sprints.current`).

Derived cache (cycle-129 FR-5): `run-checkpoint.sh derive --write` (also run by every `write`)
rewrites `.state` (canonical) and `.status` (its mirror) from the files and adds
`"derived_at": "<ISO-8601>"` and
`"derivation": {"source": "files", "stale_markers": [], "legacy_feedback": [], "sprint_ids": []}`;
`schema_version` is kept. Files without these keys are read as before. The decision table is
in the script header; `run_mode.file_authoritative: false` makes it report-only.

content.content:
### Pre-flight

0. Run `.claude/scripts/run-preflight.sh --unattended --resume` (P6 inverted: a resumable state
   passes, nothing to resume fails). Non-zero exit → surface its checklist and stop.
0a. Run `.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh derive --json` (exit 4 = no active cycle: keep the
   cache and continue). When `.drift` is true, report "files say {state}, cache said
   {cache_state}" and run `.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh derive --write` before continuing,
   so the steps below read the file-derived position (cycle-129 FR-5).
1. If `.run/state.json` doesn't exist: "ERROR: No run state found. Start a new run with `/run
   sprint-N`" → exit 1.
2. Read `.state` (canonical; `.status` is only its mirror). If not `HALTED`: "ERROR: Run is not halted (state: {state})" — if `RUNNING`, add
   "Run is already in progress. Use `/run-status` to check."; if `JACKED_OUT`, add "Run is already
   complete. Start a new run with `/run sprint-N`." → exit 1.
3. Compare `git branch --show-current` against `.branch` in state. Mismatch → "ERROR: Branch
   mismatch / Expected: {expected} / Current: {current} / Checkout the correct branch: `git
   checkout {expected}`" → exit 1.
4. Unless `--force`: check branch divergence —
   `git fetch origin "$branch" 2>&1` (never redirect stash/git diagnostic output to `/dev/null`
   per `.claude/rules/stash-safety.md`'s spirit — surface fetch failures), then compare
   `git rev-parse HEAD` against `git rev-parse "origin/$branch"`. Same → fine. If
   `git merge-base --is-ancestor "origin/$branch" HEAD` succeeds (local ahead) → fine. Otherwise
   diverged: "ERROR: Branch has diverged from remote / Local: {local} / Remote: {remote} / This
   can happen if someone else pushed, or you made changes outside Run Mode. / To force resume: `/run-resume --force`.
   / To sync first: `git pull --rebase origin {branch}`" → exit 1.
5. If `.run/circuit-breaker.json` exists and `.state == "OPEN"` and `--reset-ice` was not passed:
   show the last trip (`jq '.history[-1]'` → trigger/reason/timestamp) and instruct: "To reset and
   continue: `/run-resume --reset-ice`. To continue without reset (may halt again): `/run-resume
   --force`." → exit 1.

### Resume Execution

1. Read `run_id`, `target`, `phase`, `cycles.current` from `.run/state.json`; report them, then
   report `.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh read` (sprint / last closed task / phase, or
   "sprint granularity"). `/implement` resumes at the first open bead (`br ready`) — the
   checkpoint never overrides beads.
2. If `--reset-ice`: reset the circuit breaker —
   `jq --arg ts "$timestamp" '.state = "CLOSED" | .triggers.same_issue.count = 0 | .triggers.same_issue.last_hash = null | .triggers.no_progress.count = 0 | .triggers.cycle_count.current = 0 | .triggers.timeout.started = $ts | .reset_at = $ts'`
   on `.run/circuit-breaker.json` (`reset_at`: `derive` recomputes the counters only from rounds
   after it, so the reset holds).
3. Update `.run/state.json` atomically: `.state = "RUNNING" | del(.halt) | .timestamps.last_activity = $ts`;
   when `.run/sprint-plan-state.json` says `HALTED`, the same on it with `.status = .state` (HALTED is
   sticky in the derivation until this step clears it).
4. Report "✓ State updated to RUNNING" then resume the main loop at the recorded `phase`:
   `INIT` → restart from initialization; `IMPLEMENT` → re-run `/implement $target` then continue
   the loop; `REVIEW` → re-run `/review-sprint $target` then continue; `AUDIT` → re-run
   `/audit-sprint $target` then continue; unknown phase → start from `IMPLEMENT`.
# run-mode Sprint Plan Execution Loop (`/run sprint-plan`)

## Sprint Discovery

Try each source in priority order; use the first that returns non-empty:

1. **Priority 1 — `sprint.md` sections**: `grep -E "^## Sprint [0-9]+:" grimoires/loa/sprint.md | sed 's/## Sprint \([0-9]*\):.*/sprint-\1/' | sort -t'-' -k2 -n`.
2. **Priority 2 — `ledger.json`**: read `active_cycle` via
   `jq -r '.active_cycle' grimoires/loa/ledger.json`, then
   `jq -r --arg cycle "$active_cycle" '.cycles[] | select(.id == $cycle) | .sprints[] | .local_label' grimoires/loa/ledger.json`.
3. **Priority 3 — a2a directories**: `find grimoires/loa/a2a -maxdepth 1 -type d -name "sprint-*" | sed 's|.*/||' | sort -t'-' -k2 -n`.
4. If all three are empty: HALT — "No sprints found".

## Pre-flight

Same as `/run` (config check, then `.claude/scripts/run-preflight.sh --unattended` — nonzero →
HALT with its checklist), plus: run sprint discovery (above); if empty, HALT — "No sprints
discovered". Otherwise report the discovered sprint list.

## Main Loop

```
initialize_sprint_plan_state()
for sprint in filtered_sprints (apply --from/--to: keep sprint N iff from <= N <= to):
  1. Check .run/sprint-plan-state.json for sprint already "completed" → skip
  2. Run the single-sprint main loop above for this sprint (max_cycles, timeout from options)
  3. COMPLETE → continue to next sprint; HALTED → break outer loop, preserve state
  4. Update .run/sprint-plan-state.json (mark sprint completed, advance current, roll up metrics);
     `.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh write --sprint <next> --phase IMPLEMENT`
create_plan_pr()
update_state(state: JACKED_OUT)   # writes .state, mirrors .status: resources/completion-modes.md §Jack-out
```

State file `.run/sprint-plan-state.json` schema (`schema_version` 2 adds `checkpoint`; readers
accept 1 and 2 — a missing checkpoint means sprint granularity):
→ verbatim block: `resources/state-schemas.md` §sprint-plan-state-schema

Checkpoint discipline (cycle-125 FR-3): every write goes through `run-checkpoint.sh` (jq →
`.tmp.$$` → `mv -f` under `flock`); `/implement` writes `--task <bead-id> --phase IMPLEMENT`
after each `br close`; the loop above writes the phase changes. `run-checkpoint.sh read`
discards a checkpoint whose bead is not closed — beads remain the recovery source.

## Sprint Failure Handling

On a HALTED sprint inside the plan loop:
1. Atomically update `.run/sprint-plan-state.json`:
   `jq --arg s "$failed_sprint" --arg r "$reason" '.state = "HALTED" | .status = .state | .failure = {"sprint": $s, "reason": $r, "timestamp": (now | strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ"))}'`.

+# (.claude/data/floor.yaml lists them; tests/unit/profile-floor.bats pins it).
+# An unknown value warns and falls back to standard.
+loa:
+  profile: standard   # lean | standard | full
+
 # -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 # Ride Configuration (v1.31.0)
 # -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
@@ -551,6 +574,16 @@ run_mode:
   defaults:
     max_cycles: 20
     timeout_hours: 8
+  # Run position from files (cycle-129 FR-5): `run-checkpoint.sh derive` rebuilds
+  # .run/sprint-plan-state.json (.state canonical, .status mirrored, derived_at) and
+  # .run/circuit-breaker.json from COMPLETED markers, LOA-VERDICT trailers, the ledger
+  # and git at every checkpoint. false = report-only (the caches are written as before;
+  # the rollback key).
+  file_authoritative: true
+  # Hours after which a RUNNING run with no activity derives to INTERRUPTED, and after
+  # which a derived cache (derived_at) no longer counts as a known run position for the
+  # implement gate. Positive integer.
+  stale_hours: 12
   sprint_plan:
     branch_prefix: "feature/"
     default_branch_name: "release"
@@ -576,6 +609,34 @@ run_mode:
     # Override if your project uses a different commit convention.
     sprint_commit_pattern: '^feat\(sprint-'
 
+# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Implement gate (cycle-129 FR-4(a); hook: .claude/hooks/compliance/implement-gate.sh)
+# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# PreToolUse check on Write/Edit/NotebookEdit into the App Zone (src/, lib/, app/)
+# outside an implementation run. A write is SANCTIONED (allowed, one audit row each) by:
+#   - a RUNNING run cache (.run/sprint-plan-state.json or .run/state.json, fresh
+#     last_activity, and derived_at within run_mode.stale_hours when present);
+#   - .run/implement-active.json {skill: implement|bug, sprint, started_at} younger than
+#     two hours (`run-checkpoint.sh mark` at the start of /implement and /bug, `unmark`
+#     at the end); a stale or malformed marker is logged and does not sanction;
+#   - LOA_IMPLEMENT_GATE_OVERRIDE=1 in the session environment (audited, one row per write).
+# An unsanctioned App-Zone write is then handled by `mode`:
+#   ask        (default) asks for confirmation, as before, and logs one row per ask
+#   telemetry  logs one row to .run/audit.jsonl and allows silently

+      display_run_position_lines

@@ -689,6 +690,10 @@ main() {
     echo "───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────"
     display_providers_section
 
+    # Profile line (cycle-129 FR-9, SDD D-9.3): the effective loa.profile and explicit overrides.
+    echo ""

+
     # Guards line (cycle-129 FR-1, SDD D-1.5): register counts and the host yield.
     echo ""
     display_guards_line
@@ -931,6 +936,31 @@ display_providers_section() {
   return 0
 }
 
+# cycle-129 FR-9 (SDD D-9.3): one Profile line — the effective loa.profile and
+# the explicit keys whose value differs from it. Reads the config the Providers
+# block reads (bats-gated seam LOA_STATUS_CONFIG_FILE); the lib runs in a
+# subshell so its globals stay out of this script.
+display_profile_line() {
+  local lib="$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/profile-lib.sh" cfg line
+  if [[ ! -f "$lib" ]]; then
+    echo -e "${BOLD}Profile:${NC} unknown (lib/profile-lib.sh missing; reinstall the framework with /update-loa)"
+    return 0
+  fi
+  cfg=$(_providers_config_file)
+  line=$(
+    if [[ "$cfg" != "$CONFIG_FILE" ]]; then export LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE="$cfg"; fi
+    # shellcheck source=lib/profile-lib.sh
+    source "$lib" || exit 0
+    name=$(loa_profile 2>/dev/null) || name=standard
+    note=""
+    if [[ "$(loa_profile_source 2>/dev/null)" == "invalid" ]]; then note="unknown loa.profile, using standard; "; fi
+    ov=$(loa_profile_overrides 2>/dev/null | awk 'NF { printf "%s%s", (n++ ? ", " : ""), $0 }')
+    printf '%s (%sexplicit overrides: %s)' "${name:-standard}" "$note" "${ov:-none}"
+  ) || line=""
+  echo -e "${BOLD}Profile:${NC} ${line:-standard (explicit overrides: unavailable)}"
+  return 0
+}
+
 # cycle-129 FR-1 (SDD D-1.5): one Guards line. Counts come from the tracked structural
 # register (grimoires/loa/guards.md), the 30-day yield from the untracked
 # .run/guard-yield.json; nothing is recomputed here. Bats-gated seams:
@@ -978,6 +1008,25 @@ display_gate_line() {
   return 0
 }
 
+# cycle-129 FR-5 / FR-4(a) (SDD D-5.3): the run position the files derive against
      echo "  State: ${state}"
      [[ -n "$description" ]] && echo "  ${description}"

      # Progress bar
      local filled=$((progress / 5))
      local empty=$((20 - filled))
      printf "  Progress: ["
      printf '%0.s█' $(seq 1 $filled 2>/dev/null) || true
      printf '%0.s░' $(seq 1 $empty 2>/dev/null) || true
      printf "] %d%%\n" "$progress"

      [[ -n "$current_sprint" ]] && echo "  Current Sprint: ${current_sprint}"
      echo "  Sprints: ${completed_sprints}/${total_sprints} complete"
      display_artefacts_line
      display_run_line
      display_context_line
      display_gate_line
      display_run_position_lines

      echo ""
      echo "───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────"
      [[ -n "$suggested" ]] && echo -e " ${BOLD}Suggested:${NC} ${CYAN}${suggested}${NC}"
    else
      echo ""
      echo "  Workflow state detection unavailable"
      echo "  (workflow-state.sh not found)"
    fi

    # Providers section (cycle-125 FR-4, SDD §1.5): breakers, credential presence, CLI hops.
    echo ""
    echo "───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────"
    display_providers_section

    # Profile line (cycle-129 FR-9, SDD D-9.3): the effective loa.profile and explicit overrides.
    echo ""
    display_profile_line

    # Guards line (cycle-129 FR-1, SDD D-1.5): register counts and the host yield.
    echo ""
    display_guards_line

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# profile-lib.sh — `loa.profile` resolution (cycle-129 SDD D-9.1, §5.3;
     4	# DEC-0143, DEC-0152, DEC-0166).
     5	#
     6	# Sourced API (bash 3.2 safe; sets no shell options; every function returns 0
     7	# unless stated):
     8	#   loa_profile                     → lean | standard | full
     9	#   loa_profile_source              → explicit | default | invalid
    10	#   loa_knob <yq-path> <fallback>   → the effective value of one config key:
    11	#        the key set explicitly in the config (an explicit `false` counts —
    12	#        never `// default`, which reads false as absent), else the selected
    13	#        profile's value when the key is a profile key, else <fallback>.
    14	#        Returns 2 (printing the fallback) on a malformed path.
    15	#   loa_profile_overrides           → `key=value` lines, one per explicit
    16	#        profile key whose value differs from the selected profile's value
    17	#   loa_effective_json              → the resolved document (below)
    18	#
    19	# CLI: profile-lib.sh profile | source | knob <path> <fallback> | overrides | json
    20	#
    21	# Inputs (each has a test seam):
    22	#   config    LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE, else LOA_STATUS_CONFIG_FILE (honoured
    23	#             only under bats, like loa-status.sh), else <root>/.loa.config.yaml
    24	#   profiles  LOA_PROFILES_FILE, else <root>/.claude/data/profiles.yaml
    25	#   floor     LOA_PROFILE_FLOOR_FILE, else <root>/.claude/data/floor.yaml
    26	#   root      LOA_PROFILE_ROOT, else three directories above this file
    27	#
    28	# Cache: <root>/.run/effective-config.json (LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE overrides),
    29	# keyed on the paths and the mtime+size of the config, profiles.yaml and
    30	# floor.yaml: any edit to one of them rebuilds it on the next call, so it is
    31	# built once per session in practice. When the config is a seam (not the
    32	# repository's own file) and no cache seam is set, nothing is cached — a test
    33	# config never overwrites the repository's cache. The warm path is one stat
    34	# and one jq. The write is atomic (temp file + mv in the same directory).
    35	#
    36	# Safety: a profile key that names a floor key (floor.yaml `floor_keys`, `*`
    37	# matches one or more characters; an ancestor of a floor key also counts) is
    38	# ignored with a WARN — no profile can reach the floor. Key paths are checked
    39	# against ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+(\.[A-Za-z0-9_]+)*$ before they reach a yq expression.
    40	# Overrides and the requested profile name are control-stripped and cut.
    41	# =============================================================================
    42	
    43	_LOA_PL_SELF="${BASH_SOURCE[0]}"
    44	_LOA_PL_SELF_DIR="${_LOA_PL_SELF%/*}"
    45	[[ "$_LOA_PL_SELF_DIR" == "$_LOA_PL_SELF" ]] && _LOA_PL_SELF_DIR="."
    46	_LOA_PL_SELF_DIR="$(cd "$_LOA_PL_SELF_DIR" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)"
    47	_LOA_PL_JSON=""
    48	_LOA_PL_ID=""
    49	
    50	_loa_pl_paths() {
    51	  local root="${LOA_PROFILE_ROOT:-}"
    52	  if [[ -z "$root" ]]; then
    53	    root="$(cd "$_LOA_PL_SELF_DIR/../../.." 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)"
    54	  fi
    55	  _LOA_PL_ROOT="$root"
    56	  local default_cfg="$root/.loa.config.yaml" status_cfg=""
    57	  # LOA_STATUS_CONFIG_FILE is loa-status.sh's bats-gated seam; honour it the same way.
    58	  if [[ -n "${BATS_TEST_FILENAME:-}${BATS_VERSION:-}" ]]; then
    59	    status_cfg="${LOA_STATUS_CONFIG_FILE:-}"
    60	  fi
    61	  _LOA_PL_CFG="${LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE:-${status_cfg:-$default_cfg}}"
    62	  _LOA_PL_PROF="${LOA_PROFILES_FILE:-$root/.claude/data/profiles.yaml}"
    63	  _LOA_PL_FLOOR="${LOA_PROFILE_FLOOR_FILE:-$root/.claude/data/floor.yaml}"
    64	  if [[ -n "${LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE:-}" ]]; then
    65	    _LOA_PL_CACHE="$LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE"
    66	  elif [[ "$_LOA_PL_CFG" == "$default_cfg" ]]; then
    67	    _LOA_PL_CACHE="$root/.run/effective-config.json"
    68	  else
    69	    _LOA_PL_CACHE=""
    70	  fi
    71	}
    72	
    73	# The cache key: the three paths plus one stat line per existing file. An
    74	# empty stat output for an existing file (no usable stat) disables caching.
    75	_loa_pl_id() {
    76	  local st
    77	  st=$(stat -Lc '%n|%y|%s' -- "$_LOA_PL_CFG" "$_LOA_PL_PROF" "$_LOA_PL_FLOOR" 2>/dev/null) ||
    78	    st=$(stat -Lf '%N|%Fm|%z' -- "$_LOA_PL_CFG" "$_LOA_PL_PROF" "$_LOA_PL_FLOOR" 2>/dev/null) || true
    79	  if [[ -z "$st" ]] && [[ -e "$_LOA_PL_CFG" || -e "$_LOA_PL_PROF" ]]; then
    80	    _LOA_PL_CUR_ID=""
    81	    return 0
    82	  fi
    83	  _LOA_PL_CUR_ID="v1|$_LOA_PL_CFG|$_LOA_PL_PROF|$_LOA_PL_FLOOR|${st//$'\n'/;}"
    84	}
    85	
    86	_loa_pl_warn() { printf '[profile-lib] WARN: %s\n' "$*" >&2; }
    87	
    88	# Builds the resolved document from the three inputs into _LOA_PL_JSON.
    89	_loa_pl_build() {
    90	  local cfg='{}' prof='{}' floor='[]' out
    91	  if ! command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || ! command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    92	    _LOA_PL_JSON=""
    93	    return 1
    94	  fi
    95	  if [[ -f "$_LOA_PL_CFG" ]]; then
    96	    if ! cfg=$(yq -o=json '.' "$_LOA_PL_CFG" 2>/dev/null); then
    97	      _loa_pl_warn "$_LOA_PL_CFG does not parse; profile defaults apply"
    98	      cfg='{}'
    99	    fi
   100	  fi
   101	  if [[ -f "$_LOA_PL_PROF" ]]; then
   102	    if ! prof=$(yq -o=json '.' "$_LOA_PL_PROF" 2>/dev/null); then
   103	      _loa_pl_warn "$_LOA_PL_PROF does not parse; no profile defaults apply"
   104	      prof='{}'
   105	    fi
   106	  else
   107	    _loa_pl_warn "$_LOA_PL_PROF is missing; no profile defaults apply"
   108	  fi
   109	  if [[ -f "$_LOA_PL_FLOOR" ]]; then
   110	    floor=$(yq -o=json '.floor_keys // []' "$_LOA_PL_FLOOR" 2>/dev/null) || floor='[]'
   111	  fi
   112	  [[ -n "$cfg" ]] || cfg='{}'
   113	  [[ -n "$prof" ]] || prof='{}'
   114	  [[ -n "$floor" ]] || floor='[]'
   115	  out=$(printf '%s\n%s\n%s\n' "$cfg" "$prof" "$floor" | jq -cs --arg id "$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID" '
   116	    def render: if type == "string" then . elif type == "object" or type == "array" then tojson else tostring end;
   117	    def clean($n): render | gsub("[[:cntrl:]]"; "?") | .[0:$n];
   118	    def globre: "^" + (split("*") | map(gsub("\\."; "\\.")) | join(".+")) + "$";
   119	    (.[0] | if type == "object" then . else {} end) as $cfg |
   120	    (.[1] | if type == "object" then . else {} end) as $pf |
   121	    (.[2] | if type == "array" then map(select(type == "string")) else [] end) as $floor |

#!/usr/bin/env bats
# =============================================================================
# tests/unit/karpathy-surgical-diff.bats — cycle-129 sprint-256 Task 2.3
# (AC-2.3; PRD AC-4.3; SDD D-4.3, D-4.2a; DEC-0141)
#
# The surgical-diff hook keys its running total on the checkpoint task
# (`run-checkpoint.sh read --json`), else the sprint, else the session id;
# keeps one sanitised file per task under the state directory (at most 20);
# deletes the legacy session-long file; writes the summary the review's
# SURGICAL axis reads; and is silent when the knob is off. A fixture
# checkpoint (LOA_RUN_DIR) and a fake `br` on PATH stand in for a live run.
# =============================================================================

bats_require_minimum_version 1.5.0

setup() {
    R="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/../.." && pwd)"
    HOOK="$R/.claude/hooks/quality/karpathy-surgical-diff-check.sh"
    command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || skip "jq not available"
    command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 || skip "yq not available"
    T="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR"
    export LOA_CONFIG_OVERRIDE="$T/config.yaml"
    export KARPATHY_STATE_DIR="$T/state"
    export KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE="$T/summary.json"
    export KARPATHY_LEGACY_STATE="$T/karpathy-task-state.jsonl"
    export KARPATHY_TRAJECTORY_DIR="$T/trajectory"
    export LOA_RUN_DIR="$T/run"
    unset LOA_SESSION_ID LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE
    mkdir -p "$T/run" "$T/bin"
    printf 'karpathy_principles:\n  surgical_diff_warning: true\n  diff_lines_per_task: 5\n' > "$LOA_CONFIG_OVERRIDE"
    # Fake beads: every bead reports closed unless BR_STATUS says otherwise.
    printf '%s\n' '#!/usr/bin/env bash' 'printf "{\"status\":\"%s\"}\n" "${BR_STATUS:-closed}"' > "$T/bin/br"
    chmod +x "$T/bin/br"
    export PATH="$T/bin:$PATH"
}

# checkpoint <sprint> [task] — a schema-2 run state with that checkpoint
checkpoint() {
    jq -n --arg s "$1" --arg t "${2:-}" \
        '{schema_version: 2, state: "RUNNING",
          checkpoint: {sprint: $s, task: (if $t == "" then null else $t end), phase: "IMPLEMENT", ts: "2026-10-14T00:00:00Z"}}' \
        > "$T/run/sprint-plan-state.json"
}

# write_lines <n> [session_id] — one Write payload adding n lines
write_lines() {
    local n="$1" sid="${2:-sess-1}" content
    content=$(seq 1 "$n" | paste -sd'\n' -)
    jq -nc --arg c "$content" --arg s "$sid" \
        '{tool_name: "Write", session_id: $s, tool_input: {file_path: "/repo/src/x.sh", content: $c}}' \
        | bash "$HOOK"
}
